newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish scandal probe to seek Ciller testimony.
newsitem.headline: Turkish scandal probe to seek Ciller testimony.

text.p: Turkey's Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller will be invited to testify to a parliamentary commission about a security scandal linking the state with underworld gangs, a commission member said on Friday.
"Ciller and her husband were this week put on the list of those to be heard by the commission," deputy Yasar Topcu, from the main opposition Motherland Party, told Reuters.

The scandal erupted last November after a leading police official and a wanted gangster died together in a car crash. Travelling in the same car was an MP from Ciller's True Path Party (DYP), who was injured in the accident.
"These events occurred mostly during her term as prime minister. She must be questioned as to whether she knew anything or not," Topcu said.
Ciller was prime minister from 1993 until March 1996.
Parliament last month dropped two charges against her relating to alleged corruption at a state electricity company and a leading car maker during that period.
Topcu did not say why the commission had decided to seek testimony from Tansu Ciller's wealthy businessmen husband Ozer Ciller.
Testifying to the commission is not obligatory for those invited to give evidence.

A series of media reports following the crash have linked senior officials to far-right gangsters alleged to have carried out political killings and dirty work for the state in its fight against far-left groups and Kurdish rebels.

The injured DYP deputy Sedat Bucak and former interior minister Mehmet Agar, also from the DYP who resigned after the crash, face possible criminal charges over the scandal if their parliamentary immunity from prosecution is lifted.
Bucak, who heads a large anti-rebel Kurdish militia sponsored by the state in southeast, is being investigated on charges of concealing the wanted gangster Abdullah Catli.
Agar is being investigated on a charge of signing a false police document for Catli.
